sources.content:
# Design

## Context

See proposal.md. The view uses `registerTreeDataProvider`; groups and cards are sorted by `byUrgency`. VS Code supports reordering through a `TreeDragAndDropController` passed to `createTreeView`.

## Decisions

- **Order as key lists** in `globalState` key `sessionOrder` = `{ projects: [project], sessions: { [project]: [session key] } }`. A titled session's key is its name (stable across restarts); an untitled one, named after its folder and not unique, is keyed `id:<session id>` (found in review).
- **Reorders merge, never replace** (found in review): the new list is the displayed keys merged with stored keys not displayed (each kept after its stored predecessor), so hidden sessions and projects without live sessions keep their place.
- **Keyboard alternative** (found in review): "Move up" / "Move down" in the context menu of sessions and projects (reachable with Shift+F10) apply the same move as a drag.
- **Unreadable files** (found in review): `vscode/session-files.js` reports files without parsed events separately, and pruning keeps their hidden entries.
- **Pure helpers in `status-core.js`:** `applyOrder(items, keys, keyOf, fallback)` puts items whose key is listed first in list order, then the rest by `fallback`; `moveBefore(keys, moved, target)` returns the keys with `moved` placed before `target`, or last when `target` is absent. On a drop the view takes the keys as currently displayed, moves one, and stores the full list, so everything displayed becomes placed.
- **Drag and drop:** `createTreeView` with a controller using one mime type for this view; the drag carries the dragged element's kind, project and order key (`sessionKey`); drops are accepted only session→session or session→own project (same project) and project→project.
- **Reset:** command clears `sessionOrder`.
- **Review fixes:** one `persist(key, value)` helper awaits the update, refreshes, and shows an error message if it fails; `readSessions` skips files with no parsed events; the hidden group label becomes `Hidden (n)`.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [Two sessions with the same name in different projects] → order lists are per project, so names only need to be unique within a project, which session names are.

# Proposal

## Why

The developer wants to arrange the session view as they work: projects in their own order and sessions inside a project in their own order, instead of the automatic urgency sort that, for example, lifts an idle session they rarely use.

## What Changes

- Sessions can be dragged to a new position inside their project, and projects can be dragged among projects; a session cannot be dropped into another project.
- The developer's order wins over urgency. Colours, the status-bar jump and the next-waiting shortcut keep finding waiting sessions. Sessions and projects never placed by hand appear after the placed ones, sorted by urgency.
- "Toolkit: Reset session order" returns to automatic sorting.
- The order is stored per machine and shared by all windows.
- Fixes from the hidden-group review: storage writes report failures; an unreadable or empty session file no longer counts as new activity; the hidden group label reads "Hidden (n)".

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

None.

### Modified Capabilities

- `session-status`: manual ordering and the review fixes.

## Impact

`vscode/status-core.js`, `vscode/sessions-view.js`, `vscode/session-files.js`, `vscode/package.json`, tests, README.

# Tasks

## 1. Implementation

- [x] 1.1 Add `applyOrder` and `moveBefore` to `vscode/status-core.js` with tests
- [x] 1.2 Drag and drop controller, stored order, reset command, review fixes in `sessions-view.js`/`package.json`; verify VS Code loads it
- [x] 1.3 Document ordering in README
- [x] 1.4 Review fixes: order keys by `sessionKey` (untitled sessions by id), `mergeOrder` keeping placements of items not displayed, Move up/Move down in the context menu (`stepTarget`), unreadable session files reported by `vscode/session-files.js`; verify with tests

## 2. Acceptance

- [x] 2.1 With the developer: reorder sessions within a project and projects, see a cross-project drop refused, see the order in a second window, reset

# Proposal

## Why

Bug reported by the developer: in a plain `claude` tab they used `/resume` to continue a chat started in another terminal. The tab now runs the resumed session, but the old `<project>-claude` card stayed, and the resumed chat's card said "not in a toolkit tab". `/resume` (and `/clear`) switch the session inside the same Claude process without a SessionEnd, and the view links cards to tabs by session name, which changes on resume, clear and rename.

## What Changes

- The status hook records the Claude process id (`CLAUDE_PID`) with each session.
- Each window publishes the process ids of the tabs it opened; cards are linked to tabs by process id first, name second.
- When a newer session reports the same process id, older sessions of that process are no longer shown.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

None.

### Modified Capabilities

- `session-status`: tab identity by process, superseded sessions.

## Impact

`status/status-hook.mjs`, `vscode/status-core.js`, `vscode/sessions-view.js`, `vscode/core.js`, `vscode/extension.js`, tests.

# Tasks

## 1. Fix

- [x] 1.1 Record `pid` in the hook; add `latestPerProcess` and pid matching in `status-core.js`; verify with hook and core tests
- [x] 1.2 Publish tab process ids, match focus and close by pid in `sessions-view.js`; verify VS Code loads it

- [x] 1.3 Rename the active plain tab to the session running in its process, and check the plain tab by its tracked terminal so a renamed tab is not opened twice; verify with tests

## 2. Acceptance

- [x] 2.1 With the developer: `/resume` in the plain tab leaves one card, linked to the tab and focusable, and the tab title shows the resumed chat

# Design

## Decisions

- **Rename decision** `plainTabRename({ sessionName, lastApplied, tabName, otherTabNames, defaultSessionName })` returns the new name only when the session name exists and differs from the last name the extension applied, from the current tab name and from the tab's own default session name (`<project>-claude`, so a fresh tab stays `claude`), and is neither `coordinator`, `claude` nor the name of another open tab of the window. The view keeps the last applied session name per plain terminal (`WeakMap`) and records it whenever the session name is seen, renamed or not, so a name typed by the developer survives until the session changes.
- **Order pruning** takes the unreadable ids from the last read and keeps their `id:` keys.
- **Move guard:** `move(undefined, …)` returns.
- **Hook folder name** splits the project path on both `/` and `\` (found running the suite in a Linux container: Node's `basename` splits only on the platform's separator).

## Limitations

- The rename wiring in `sessions-view.js` (last-applied tracking, other tab names, active-terminal guard) is covered only through the pure decision function; the developer pushed before trying it by hand. Follow-up: try a typed tab name and a `/resume` in the plain tab.

# Proposal

## Why

The last reviews left small issues: the plain tab's automatic rename overrides a name the developer typed and can take a name that identifies another tab; a reorder while a session file is briefly unreadable can drop that session's placement; Move up/Move down throws without a selected item; a few documents drifted from the code.

## What Changes

- The plain tab is renamed only when the session running in it changes, never to `coordinator`, `claude` or the name of another open tab; a name typed by the developer stays until the next session change.
- Order pruning keeps keys of sessions whose files are briefly unreadable.
- Move up/Move down do nothing without an item.
- The status hook takes the project folder name from either path separator, so it is the same on Windows, macOS and Linux.
- Layout and document corrections (archived `add-manual-order` and `fix-session-tab-identity` records).

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

None.

### Modified Capabilities

- `session-status`: plain tab rename rules and order pruning.

## Impact

`vscode/status-core.js`, `vscode/sessions-view.js`, `status/status-hook.mjs`, tests, archived OpenSpec documents.

# Spec Delta

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Plain tab rename respects the developer

The plain tab SHALL be renamed only when the session running in its Claude process differs from the last session name applied to it and from the tab's own default session (`<project>-claude`, so a fresh tab stays `claude`), and SHALL NOT take `coordinator`, `claude` or the name of another open tab of the window.

#### Scenario: Manual name kept

- **WHEN** the developer renames the plain tab by hand while the same session keeps running
- **THEN** the tab keeps the developer's name

#### Scenario: New chat

- **WHEN** the developer then runs `/resume` and picks another chat
- **THEN** the tab takes the new chat's name

#### Scenario: Reserved or taken name

- **WHEN** the resumed chat is named `coordinator`, `claude` or like another open tab
- **THEN** the plain tab keeps its current name

### Requirement: Project folder on every platform

The hook SHALL take the project folder name as the last segment of the project path split on both `/` and `\`, so the same result holds on Windows, macOS and Linux.

#### Scenario: Windows path on macOS or Linux

- **WHEN** the hook receives `C:\repos\rehlko-portal` on a POSIX system
- **THEN** the folder name is `rehlko-portal`

### Requirement: Order pruning keeps unreadable sessions

Pruning the stored order SHALL treat sessions whose files are present but unreadable as existing.

#### Scenario: Briefly unreadable file

- **WHEN** the developer reorders a project while a placed hand-started session's file cannot be read
- **THEN** that session keeps its placement

# Tasks

## 1. Implementation

- [x] 1.1 New `plainTabRename` rules and order pruning with unreadable ids in `status-core.js`, with tests
- [x] 1.2 Last-applied tracking, blocked names, move guard and layout in `sessions-view.js`
- [x] 1.3 Correct the archived `add-manual-order` and `fix-session-tab-identity` documents
- [x] 1.4 Split the hook's project folder name on both separators, with a test using Windows and POSIX paths; verify the suite on Windows and in a Linux container

Manual check in VS Code of the rename wiring (typed name kept, `/resume` followed) was not done before the push; the developer chose to push and will report problems. Tracked as a limitation and follow-up in design.md.
